reflection: Results are not visible in this run, so I rely on the priors from the notebook: the existing useful factors are volatility (10d, 20d), MSFT_return_1d and NVDA 5d returns. I will build on volatility-regime and peer-lead themes, using different normalizations (log, zscore) and new combinations. I will also add some new ideas: volume-price divergence, QQQ trend state, and 2-day reversal. I will drop plain ratios that duplicate existing factors.

factors.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol20_log
factors.hypothesis: The 60d denominator likely spans regime changes and is too slow; a 20d baseline gives a cleaner short-term vol expansion/contraction signal that is less collinear with existing vol levels.

factors.name: msft_ret_minus_qqq_ret_1d
factors.hypothesis: MSFT 1d return is useful but largely market beta; removing QQQ isolates MSFT idiosyncratic strength, which may carry lead/lag information for Apple.

factors.name: aapl_two_day_reversal_vol_adj
factors.hypothesis: Short-term moves scaled by recent vol capture overreaction mean reversion across regimes with very different volatility.

factors.name: qqq_close_to_ma20_vs_vol
factors.hypothesis: Vol-normalized QQQ trend deviation describes the market state (stretched vs. neutral) comparable across years.

factors.name: aapl_vol_price_divergence_vs_qqq_volume
factors.hypothesis: Pairs with Apple's own vol regime: when market volume is elevated relative to Apple's, the move is market-driven, changing how vol expansion predicts direction.

factors.name: aapl_vs_peer_3d_relative_strength
factors.hypothesis: Apple's 3d lag versus the peer average complements the 1d peer-lead signal: catch-up potential when peers led over a slightly longer window.
